tasks.short: Identify disease causes, development, morphology and clinical significance

steps.what: Collect and verify the actual case identity, specimen context and available clinical and laboratory evidence
inputs: Clinical history supplied by referring clinicians
Specimen and test records produced by laboratory staff in the pathology information system, defined as OPS_SYSTEM
outputs: Pathologist-verified case sources and explicit evidence gaps

steps.what: Stage exact case identifiers and selected existing source-record fields into the current draft case worksheet
inputs: Specific source records verified in s1
Explicit field and specimen identifier mapping
outputs: Staged case fields with original source links and unmatched fields marked

steps.what: Identify disease etiology, pathogenesis, morphological change and clinical significance from the actual evidence
inputs: Actual case materials and verified evidence
Pathologist's subject expertise
outputs: Pathologist's disease assessment and stated limitations

steps.what: Write the actual case assessment and check the complete case record, source fields and diagnostic wording
inputs: Human assessment from s3
Staged fields and original sources

steps.what: Save the exact checked case assessment record
inputs: Exact complete record from s4
outputs: Saved assessment with its actual review and release status

tasks.design: Configure {OPS_SYSTEM} to stage exact existing case fields where the pathologist still transfers them manually. The pathologist performs the entire disease assessment and writes and checks the complete case record before saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: Some case worksheets may require repeated exact-field transfer from source records.
tasks.enabler_now: Native field mappings can stage those fields with source and specimen identifiers intact.
tasks.still_hard: Disease mechanisms and clinical significance require medical interpretation of the actual evidence.
tasks.human_edge: Integrate morphology and clinical context and recognise uncertainty.

ambition.what: Reduce demonstrated administrative case-field transfer only.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: pathology record systems can map exact structured case fields while diagnostic interpretation remains the pathologist's work.

assumptions: Conditional episode with an existing case worksheet and actual manual source-field transfer, not an observed baseline or an added report after every thought.

Referring clinicians and laboratory staff produce source records in their normal work. Pathologist case collection, identity checking and missing-data assessment are counted in s1; no free newly captured or normalized evidence feed.
Native configuration first; existing automatic case assembly earns zero new saving. Unmatched identifiers, ambiguous material and missing fields stay manual; no AI diagnostic inference.
Actual assessment writing and full final check are retained in s4. Saving is negligible and fully retained, and does not silently release a report or order treatment.
If final report release is part of the actual episode, add its separate checked send action. Deduplicate the same case assembly and assessment record with 17191 rather than claim both savings.
All 100 illustrative focal effort points: gross transfer saving 15 less upkeep 2 gives net 13.
unknowns: Whether any such field transfer remains manual in the actual pathology system
research_questions: Which exact case fields are still re-entered by the pathologist after native integration?

already_counted.description: Case verification, complete disease interpretation, actual record writing and final checking

incremental.description: Maintain and validate exact case-field mappings

approvals.approved_version: Exact complete case assessment checked in s4; any edit requires recheck

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Conditional manual source-field transfer saving 15 less upkeep 2; zero where the native system already performs it.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Find current pathology literature and relevant professional or conference material using the actual learning question
inputs: Pathologist's current learning needs
Actual library and professional repository records, defined as OTHER
outputs: Candidate real publications and professional material

steps.what: Read current literature and critically assess pathology findings, methods and limitations
inputs: Actual publications selected from s1

steps.what: Talk with colleagues about actual developments and their uncertainties
inputs: Actual professional questions and colleagues' perspectives

steps.what: Participate in actual pathology professional organizations or conferences
inputs: Actual professional event and participants

tasks.design: Configure native searches and saved queries in the existing {OTHER} scientific library. Reading, critical appraisal, colleague discussions and professional participation remain with the pathologist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated discovery queries can consume time before actual reading.
tasks.enabler_now: Native search filters can reuse explicit subject queries.
tasks.still_hard: Understanding evidence quality and relevance requires specialist appraisal.
tasks.human_edge: Question findings and learn from professional discussion.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: saved scientific-library queries can reduce repeated discovery effort without replacing full reading or critical appraisal.

assumptions: Illustrative mix of actual continuing-learning activities, not an observed duty distribution or time-share prior. Publication sources are produced by their authors; pathologist query formation and source checking remain in s1.
Native features first. Existing saved searches earn no new saving; no model-generated citations or automated exclusion of unread papers.
No new reading digest, learning record, conference registration send or report is invented. Actual completion records, if required in the observed process, must be added after real participation.
All 100 illustrative focal effort points: gross discovery saving 6 less upkeep 1 gives net 5.
unknowns: Current search practice and actual learning mix
research_questions: Which repeated discovery queries remain manual after existing library tools?

already_counted.description: Retained source discovery and full critical reading

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Conditional discovery saving 6 minus upkeep 1; reading and professional exchange fully retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Consult with physicians on tests, interpretation and treatment questions

steps.what: Find and verify the actual consultation question and relevant case context
inputs: Physician's actual question
Existing laboratory and clinical case records in the pathology information system, defined as OPS_SYSTEM
outputs: Checked consultation context with evidence gaps marked

steps.what: Consult directly with physicians about ordering and interpreting tests or providing treatments using the actual evidence
inputs: Checked context from s1
Physician's clinical concerns
outputs: Human clinical consultation and clearly expressed limitations

steps.what: Capture the actual required consultation note and check its complete clinical wording and case identity
inputs: Actual discussion and clinical conclusions from s2

steps.what: Save the exact checked consultation note
inputs: Exact final note from s3

tasks.design: Configure native case lookup and fixed identifier fields in {OPS_SYSTEM}. The pathologist performs the clinical consultation and captures and checks its actual note before saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: Case navigation and repeated identifier entry can interrupt consultation preparation and recording.
tasks.enabler_now: Native case views and note fields can reduce navigation and repeated fixed-field entry.
tasks.still_hard: Clinical context and the implications of test choices remain expert work.
tasks.human_edge: Explain uncertainty and collaborate with the treating physician.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native case lookup and fixed note fields can support consultation administration while clinical judgement and actual note writing remain human.

assumptions: Conditional consultation episode with an actual required note, not invented documentation after every informal exchange. Clinicians and laboratory staff produce existing case records; pathologist context checking and actual discussion capture are counted in s1-s3.
Native features first; existing case views earn no new saving. s3 reduces only fixed identifiers, retaining clinical wording and the full final check.

No generated test recommendation, automatic interpretation, prescription, test order or treatment command. Any actual order requires a separate final-version clinical check and gated action with its labour added.
Same-system save is negligible and fully retained. All 100 illustrative focal points: gross 3 plus 1.9 equals 4.9; upkeep 1 gives net 3.9.
unknowns: Actual consultation-note practice and current native fields
research_questions: Is repeated identifier entry still material after current case-linked note features?

already_counted.description: Case checking and retained actual note capture and complete final verification

incremental.description: Maintain case view and fixed note fields

approvals.approved_version: Exact complete consultation note checked in s3; any edit requires recheck

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Conditional lookup and fixed-field saving 4.9 less upkeep 1; all clinical consultation and substantive note work retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Analyze and interpret pathology test results and record findings

steps.what: Collect and verify patient and specimen identity, test context, source results and limitations for the actual case
inputs: Results and quality context produced by laboratory staff
Ordering clinician's case context in the pathology information system, defined as OPS_SYSTEM
outputs: Verified source records and explicitly identified missing or questionable evidence

steps.what: Stage exact verified result values, units and specimen identifiers from source records into the draft report fields
inputs: Specific source records verified in s1
Explicit field mappings preserving original units and qualifiers
outputs: Staged report fields linked to original results, with any mismatches held

steps.what: Analyze and interpret the actual microbial, parasite, urine, hormonal, FNA or PCR results in their clinical context
inputs: Actual verified test evidence and case context

steps.what: Write the actual interpretation and check the entire final report, source values, identifiers and intended recipient
inputs: Human interpretation from s3
Staged fields and original sources
outputs: Exact complete checked report and recipient

steps.what: Commit the exact checked report to the case record
inputs: Exact report checked in s4

steps.what: Release the exact checked report to the ordering clinician through the existing report channel
inputs: Exact final report and recipient checked in s4
outputs: Released report to the actual intended clinician

tasks.design: Configure native {OPS_SYSTEM} exact-field staging only where the pathologist still transfers result fields manually. The pathologist interprets all results and writes and checks the complete report before the separate commit and release actions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Some report workflows repeat exact source-value transcription.
tasks.enabler_now: Native mappings can stage selected source fields with their original units, qualifiers and identifiers.
tasks.still_hard: Clinical meaning, conflicts and limitations require specialist interpretation.
tasks.human_edge: Integrate test evidence and context and recognise when a result cannot support a conclusion.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: laboratory record systems can stage exact structured report fields with traceability, while pathologists retain test interpretation and final report responsibility.

assumptions: Representative interpreted-report episode, not a measured baseline for every listed test type. Laboratory personnel produce actual test records; pathologist collection and identity, context and evidence checking are counted in s1.

Native configuration first. Existing instrument imports and native report fields are baseline; if equivalent staging already exists, the new saving is zero. No free new test capture, OCR, inferred units or normalized feed.
Unmatched specimens, changed units, ambiguous results or missing qualifiers stop staging and remain human work. No diagnostic or treatment interpretation is automated.
Actual report authoring and full final checking remain in s4. Commit and release each require the same exact complete final version; any edit or recipient change requires another s4 check.

The existing release channel is retained, with no new external connection. Commit and release bookkeeping allocations earn no saving. Deduplicate the same case field transfer and report work shared with 17187.
All 100 illustrative focal effort points: gross field-transfer saving 20 less upkeep 3 gives net 17.
unknowns: Actual remaining manual transfer and report release controls
research_questions: Which source fields are manually transcribed by the pathologist after existing laboratory interfaces?

already_counted.description: Source verification, entire clinical interpretation and actual report writing and final checking

incremental.description: Maintain and validate exact result-field mappings against source schema changes

approvals.approved_version: Exact complete report checked in s4; edits invalidate the check
Exact report and intended recipient checked in s4; report or recipient changes require recheck

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Conditional manual result-field transfer saving 20 minus upkeep 3; zero where native staging already operates.
